hypothesis.statement: At least one preregistered deterministic coordinate predicate family preserves nonvacuous valid structured-embedding support across 5-8 bit random curves and improves retained final support per constrained label over matched hash-ranked x-fiber controls.
hypothesis.mechanism: Coordinate order can correlate the EC evaluations of forced degree-two and balanced degree-four formal multisets. If that correlation reduces semantic closure conflicts without suppressing the final 4F+4F sumset, an injective order ideal can retain more final support at the same factor-base size and structured-label density than a symmetry-matched random x-fiber set.
assumptions: MODEL-BOUND: a valid partial operation is evidence inside the structured generic-group formalism, not a lower bound or algorithm for conventional curve coordinates.
TOY-EVIDENCE: q has only 5-8 bits and cannot establish a cryptographic exponent.
HEURISTIC: the selected curve sampler and predicate families are probes of family persistence, not a representative measure over all curves or all coordinate predicates.
UNTESTED: the branch-and-bound support upper bound is strong enough to close most rows inside the proposed budget.
NOVELTY-UNVERIFIED: no claim of a new theorem or attack is authorized without a broader literature review.

predictions.minimum_effect: one fixed coordinate family has median ratio at least 0.25 in every 5-8 bit stratum

predictions.metric: retained final support per constrained label versus matched hash-x controls
predictions.minimum_effect: the same family has at least 1.10x the paired null median in at least three of four bit strata and a positive sign in at least 75 percent of exact curve-B pairs
at least 90 percent of coordinate and matched-null rows have zero primary gap; every remaining row has gap at most max(1, ceil(0.05q))
all interpreted rows pass every exact axiom and expose zero direct final-layer edges

instances: two deterministic accepted curves for each q bit size in {5,6,7,8}
the frozen EXP-SGCP-EMBED-001 p=19,a=2,b=9,q=23 fixture as a regression control

falsification_conditions: After valid and sufficiently resolved runs, no single coordinate family meets both the persistence and matched-null advantage predictions.
The median retained-to-raw support ratio of every coordinate family is below 0.10 in at least three bit strata with zero-gap primary certificates.
A purported valid embedding fails injectivity, associativity, unique factorization, compatibility, acyclicity, source recovery, or final-edge exclusion under independent reconstruction.
The optimizer reports a lower bound above an independently enumerated optimum or an upper bound below a known feasible incumbent.
A matched control differs in factor-base cardinality, x-fiber multiplicity, curve, B, or optimizer budget.
Any builder-visible artifact contains scalar indices or a discrete-log table.
interpretation_limits: Failure rejects or weakens only these curves, sizes, predicates, and the balanced degree-four order-ideal construction.
Success would be a toy coordinate-structure signal, not an index-calculus relation generator.
No fitted exponent is allowed from four tiny bit sizes.
The experiment does not measure relation rank, linear algebra, factor-base logarithms, individual descent, fixed-curve preprocessing crossover, or rho cost.
The SGGM hard distribution and class-wide tightness result do not imply that a high-delta coordinate embedding yields an attack on the conventional encoding.
